# simple-liquid-glass

> React and framework-agnostic liquid glass with automatic iOS WebGL refraction.
> Select `renderer="webgl"` for Android/desktop. WebGL needs an explicit sibling background.
> React 16.8–19, SSR-safe. Approximately 29 KB React / 22 KB custom element, Brotli,
> including bundled HTML capture. No additional renderer installation.

This file is written for LLMs/agents: it contains the complete public API, copy-paste recipes, and
the constraints needed to use the library correctly and autonomously. When in doubt, prefer the
patterns here over guessing. See README.md for current integration examples.

## Install

```bash
npm install simple-liquid-glass
```

Peer deps: `react` and `react-dom` (16.8 – 19). The web component needs no React.

## Entry points (exports)

- `simple-liquid-glass` → `LiquidGlass` (default and named export). Types: `LiquidGlassProps`,
  `LiquidGlassHandle`, `LiquidPreset` (`'ripple' | 'flow' | 'wobble'`), `LensMode`
  (`'classic' | 'convex' | 'shift' | 'rim'`).
- `simple-liquid-glass/interactive` → `LiquidGlassInteractive`, `usePointerElastic(ref, options)`.
  Types: `LiquidGlassInteractiveProps`, `PointerElasticOptions`, `RippleEffect` (`'ripple' | 'drop'`),
  `LiquidTrigger` (`'always' | 'hover' | 'press'`).
- `simple-liquid-glass/web-component` → side-effect import; registers the `<liquid-glass>` custom
  element. Also exports `defineLiquidGlass(tag?)` and `LiquidGlassElement`.
- `simple-liquid-glass/engine` (public since 5.7.0, `@experimental`, `ENGINE_API = 1`) → `getGlassEngine()`, a
  framework-agnostic custom-material API. See "Engine API (experimental)" below.
- `simple-liquid-glass/next` (6.0) → `createGlassHost()`: glass drawn from a worker, the scene as data, springs in
  the renderer. `simple-liquid-glass/next/stack` → the same API plus layers stacked in one canvas. See "Worker
  renderer (6.0)" below.

## How refraction works — and the #1 thing to get right

iOS/iPadOS automatically uses WebGL, including Chrome/Firefox on iOS. `renderer="webgl"`
opts Android and desktop into the same pipeline. `renderer="svg"` selects the existing SVG path
on supported non-iOS browsers. `effectMode="blur"`/`"off"` take precedence everywhere.
WebGL requires a sibling `backdropRef` or `backdropSelector`, never an ancestor of the glass.
It shares the package's lens maps and controls. Direct video/canvas sources are live; HTML is
cached and automatically refreshed for DOM mutations. Use `backdropVersion` or the imperative
`refreshBackdrop(): Promise<void>` for external stylesheet changes. Nested media in HTML is not
live. CORS restrictions apply. Capture/context failures use blur with diagnostic reasons.
iOS, desktop Safari and Firefox always use WebGL (they can't run SVG backdrop filters); Chromium
opts in with `renderer="webgl"`. Client-mounted glass stays transparent until its renderer is
ready (max 400ms); `reveal="immediate"` opts out. Animate `transform`, not `opacity`, on glass
ancestors: an opacity ancestor blanks Chromium's backdrop-filter until the fade ends.

## `<LiquidGlass>` props (React core)

| prop | type | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `renderer` | `'auto' \| 'svg' \| 'webgl'` | `'auto'` | iOS uses WebGL unless blur/off |
| `backdropRef` | RefObject<HTMLElement> | — | explicit sibling backdrop |
| `backdropSelector` | string | — | selector alternative |
| `backdropVersion` | string \| number | — | refresh HTML capture |
| `maxScale` | number | — | cap the WebGL drawing scale (device px per CSS px), e.g. 1.5 on phones |
| `children` | ReactNode | — | content inside the glass |
| `mode` | `'preset' \| 'custom'` | `'preset'` | preset applies tuned defaults; props still override |
| `scale` | number | `160` | displacement strength (negative inverts the bend) |
| `radius` | number | `50` | border radius (px) |
| `border` | number | `0.05` | border thickness 0–0.5 |
| `lightness` | number | `53` | glass lightness 0–100 |
| `displace` | number | `5` | displacement-map blur amount |
| `alpha` | number | `0.9` | glass alpha 0–1 |
| `blur` | number | `0` | post blur |
| `dispersion` | number | `50` | chromatic dispersion |
| `saturation` | number | `140` | CSS saturate() % |
| `aberrationIntensity` | number | `0` | chromatic aberration multiplier |
| `frost` | number | `0.1` | frost intensity 0–1 |
| `borderColor` | string | `rgba(120,120,120,0.7)` | gradient border color |
| `glassColor` | string | `rgba(255,255,255,0.4)` | must be semi-transparent |
| `background` | string | — | solid/gradient; auto made semi-transparent |
| `autoTextColor` | boolean | `false` | auto pick text color from background luminance |
| `textOnDark` / `textOnLight` | string | `#ffffff` / `#111111` | text colors for autoTextColor |
| `forceTextColor` | boolean | `false` | force computed text color on descendants |
| `angle` | number | `0` | **3.0** refraction direction in degrees; positive = clockwise; shape-adapted so it's faithful on any aspect. Chromium SVG path. |
| `shapeAdapt` | boolean | `true` | **3.0** aspect-faithful + isotropic refraction (glass cut to the element's shape). `false` = legacy ≤2.x map. |
| `lens` | `'classic' \| 'convex' \| 'shift' \| 'rim'` | `'classic'` | **3.0** displacement field: classic radial / dome magnifier / uniform offset / clear-center rim |
| `lensStrength` | number | `1` | **3.0** lens magnitude (0 = off) |
| `lensCenter` | `[number, number]` | `[0.5, 0.5]` | **3.0** lens center (0–1) for convex/rim |
| `liquid` | `'ripple' \| 'flow' \| 'wobble' \| false` | `false` | **3.0** real animated refraction (Chromium; in-view + reduced-motion gated) |
| `liquidSpeed` | number | `1` | **3.0** animation rate |
| `liquidScale` | number | preset | **3.0** distortion amplitude (px) |
| `quality` | `'low' \| 'standard' \| 'high' \| 'extreme'` | `'low'` | map resolution / pass count. `low` = clean single-pass; `standard`+ add 3-pass chromatic aberration |
| `autodetectquality` | boolean | `false` | pick quality from device performance |
| `mobileFallback` | `'css-only' \| 'svg'` | css-only on mobile | mobile render strategy |
| `effectMode` | `'auto' \| 'svg' \| 'blur' \| 'off'` | `'auto'` | force a strategy |
| `className` / `style` | — | — | standard; plus any HTML div attributes |

Ref (`LiquidGlassHandle`): `{ element: HTMLDivElement | null; getQuality(): quality }`.

## `<LiquidGlassInteractive>` — extra props (import from `simple-liquid-glass/interactive`)

Extends all `LiquidGlassProps` and adds pointer reactivity:

| prop | type | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `elasticity` | number | `0.15` | how far the glass leans toward the cursor (0 = rigid) |
| `maxShift` | number | `18` | max lean translate (px) |
| `stiffness` / `damping` | number | `0.18` / `0.78` | spring tuning |
| `specular` | boolean | `false` | pointer-tracked specular highlight (opt-in) |
| `followPointer` | boolean | `false` | a refractive bump that distorts the backdrop toward the cursor |
| `clickRipple` | `boolean \| 'ripple' \| 'drop'` | `false` | real water-like ripple on click (`true` = `'ripple'`; `'drop'` = droplet-in-water rings). Lag-free, compositor-driven, reduced-motion-aware |
| `rippleIntensity` | number | `1` | ripple brightness/reach |
| `liquidTrigger` | `'always' \| 'hover' \| 'press'` | `'always'` | when `liquid` animates (hover/press stay idle/zero-cost until interaction) |

Also: `usePointerElastic(ref, options)` — apply the elastic spring to any `LiquidGlassHandle` ref.

## `<liquid-glass>` web-component attributes (kebab-case, all optional)

`radius`, `frost`, `blur`, `saturation`, `displace`, `scale`, `border-color`, `lightness`, `alpha`,
`angle`, `shape-adapt` (`"false"` to disable), `lens`, `lens-strength`, `lens-center` (`"x,y"`),
`liquid`, `liquid-speed`, `liquid-scale`.

The custom element supports `renderer`, `backdrop-selector`, `backdrop-version`, `max-scale`, `effect-mode`,
`lens-profile`, `strength`, and `dispersion` in addition to the attributes above. iOS automatically
uses WebGL with an explicit source. `renderer="webgl"` opts other platforms in. It exposes
`refreshBackdrop(): Promise<void>` and `data-glass-strategy`/`data-glass-reason`.

Note: pointer interaction props (`followPointer`, `clickRipple`, `rippleIntensity`, `liquidTrigger`,
elasticity) are **React-only** (`LiquidGlassInteractive`) — they are NOT web-component attributes.
Give the element an explicit size and place it over a background.

## Recipes

### React — basic
```tsx
import { LiquidGlass } from 'simple-liquid-glass'

<LiquidGlass radius={24} style={{ width: 320, height: 180 }}>
  <div style={{ padding: 20 }}>Frosted, refractive glass</div>
</LiquidGlass>
```

### React — lens modes + directional angle (3.0)
```tsx
<LiquidGlass lens="convex" lensStrength={1.2} style={{ width: 200, height: 200 }} />
<LiquidGlass lens="shift" angle={30} style={{ width: 420, height: 64 }} /> {/* navbar */}
<LiquidGlass lens="rim" style={{ width: 160, height: 160 }} />
```

### React — real animated "liquid" refraction (3.0)
```tsx
<LiquidGlass liquid="ripple" liquidSpeed={1} style={{ width: 320, height: 200 }}>
  {/* backdrop genuinely warps; pauses off-screen + on prefers-reduced-motion; Chromium */}
</LiquidGlass>
```

### React — interactive: follow pointer + click ripples (3.0)
```tsx
import { LiquidGlassInteractive } from 'simple-liquid-glass/interactive'

<LiquidGlassInteractive elasticity={0.3} followPointer clickRipple="drop">
  Move me, then click for a water-drop ripple
</LiquidGlassInteractive>
```

### Vue / Svelte / Astro / plain HTML — web component
```html
<script type="module"
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/simple-liquid-glass/web-component"></script>

<liquid-glass radius="20" frost="0.15" lens="convex" angle="20"
  style="width:320px;height:200px;display:block">
  Glass anywhere
</liquid-glass>
```

### Next.js / SSR
SSR-safe out of the box — it only touches the DOM in effects. Use it in client components; no
`'use client'` gymnastics needed beyond your normal component boundaries.

## Constraints & gotchas (read before generating code)

- **Always provide an explicit sibling backdrop for WebGL.** Do not point at document.body or
  another ancestor of the glass. HTML capture is not a browser screenshot and does not include
  unrelated overlapping layers. Direct video/canvas sources are required for live media.
- **`liquid` and `followPointer`/`clickRipple` are GPU-real and gated**: animate only while on-screen,
  pause on `prefers-reduced-motion`, Chromium SVG path; treat `liquid` as a per-element design choice,
  not for hundreds of cards. `liquidTrigger: 'hover' | 'press'` costs nothing until interaction.
- **`shapeAdapt` defaults to `true` in 3.0** and changes how non-square lenses look at `angle: 0`
  versus 2.x (square lenses are unchanged). Set `shapeAdapt={false}` for the exact legacy map.
- **`glassColor` must be semi-transparent** (rgba/hsla/hex-with-alpha); opaque values fall back to frost.
- Give the element an explicit size; the effect fills 100% of its box.
- Many glass instances? They auto-drop their `backdrop-filter` when off-screen (IntersectionObserver).
- `clickRipple` / `rippleIntensity` / `followPointer` / `liquidTrigger` are on `LiquidGlassInteractive`
  only (the `/interactive` import), not the base component or the web component.

## Shared page backdrop (5.3.0)
Import LiquidGlassScene from simple-liquid-glass/backdrop and wrap page sections plus glass. WebGL surfaces without explicit backdropRef/backdropSelector bind automatically; explicit sources always win. iOS auto-selects WebGL; Android/desktop use renderer="webgl". The provider shares captures, not WebGL contexts. Automatic surfaces are excluded without removing layout space; explicitly sourced glass remains capturable. simple-liquid-text 0.3.0 uses the same provider. Divide long pages into direct-child sections; avoid sticky/parallax HTML inside cached regions. Cross-origin content must permit capture.

Experimental (5.5, unstable API): import { createExperimentalScene } from 'simple-liquid-glass/experimental'; createExperimentalScene(overlay, panels, source, { radius, blur, liquidGL }) renders analytical liquidGL refraction for a fixed list of flat, axis-aligned panels through one shared WebGL canvas composited below all overlay content. Returns { canvas, refresh(), status(), destroy() }. No nested clips, interleaved z-order, rotation or glass-through-glass; recreate it when panels change.

## Engine API (experimental)
Public in simple-liquid-glass 5.7.0 with ESM, CommonJS and TypeScript exports. Install
`simple-liquid-glass@~5.7.0`; no local alias is required. Types and behaviour may change in a minor release
while ENGINE_API stays 1. Review the changelog before moving to another minor.
import { getGlassEngine } from 'simple-liquid-glass/engine'. No React import. getGlassEngine() returns the page's
GlassEngine singleton (null on the server or without WebGL), shared by every bundle of the package through
ENGINE_API (currently 1). engine.defineMaterial({ id, fragment(caps), uniforms?, samplers?, inputs?, draw(ctx,
params), reset? }) compiles a private fragment shader that defines `vec4 slg_shade(vec2 p)` (premultiplied colour
at view point p, CSS px, y down) behind the stable slg_* prelude: slg_view, slg_scale, slg_origin, slg_viewport,
slg_time, slg_point(), slg_toScreen(p), slg_hasBackdrop(), slg_backdrop(screen), slg_hasUnder(), slg_under(screen).
draw(ctx, params) sets ctx.uniform / ctx.uniformArray / ctx.bind / ctx.resource(resource) and calls
ctx.draw(rects?) (no rects = the whole surface; rects = view-space CSS-px boxes, scissored within one
gl.viewport widened once for the whole call to the union of the view and every rect when one reaches past it —
so a rect may legally extend past the surface's own view, the G2 bleed gap, without slg_origin/slg_view/
slg_scale ever changing, so slg_point() stays identical to the unpadded case everywhere, including a shape a
material positions in surface coordinates like an SDF slot; a bug where a rect could not actually reach past
the view, and a regression from its first fix moving slg_origin per rect and shifting such shapes, are both
fixed and covered by conformance tests, see the changelog). ctx.uniform(name, ...values) detects the
uniform's GLSL type (getActiveUniform, once per program) and sends
int/bool/sampler2D/samplerCube through uniformNi, float/vecN through uniformNf — a G1 fix: uniformNf alone raises
GL_INVALID_OPERATION for a non-float uniform. ctx.uniformArray(name, values, components) sets a whole GLSL array
uniform (uniform vec4 uRect[8]) in one call, components 1-4 being the GLSL type's arity; same type detection and
per-program location cache as uniform(), but not value-diffed (array data is expected to change every draw). It returns
'drawn' | 'unchanged' | 'pending' | 'resized': 'pending' still presents the frame and asks again next frame (a
backdrop still loading, the G3 liveness/draw-result protocol); 'resized' redraws now with bleed() re-read.
engine.defineResource({ id, create(gl), dispose? }) plus ctx.resource(resource) give one instance per WebGL
context, recreated lazily after a context loss — the G10 gap.
engine.createSurface({ host, material, params, backdrop?, backdropVersion?, bleed?, maxScale?, composition?,
layer?, active?, onStatus? }) draws one region, either into its own presentation canvas (sharing the package's one
pooled WebGL context) or, by default ('auto'), into the nearest enclosing Layer's shared canvas if `host` sits
inside one; `layer` names one explicitly, `composition: 'own'` opts out even inside a layer's root. backdrop is an
HTMLElement (<video>/<canvas> sampled in place, anything else captured through the existing HTML-capture pipeline,
loaded lazily as a separate chunk), { scene: true } for the nearest LiquidGlassScene, or { source: id } for a
registered BackdropSource (G12). surface.update(partial) marks it dirty; surface.diagnostics() reports composition
('own' | 'layer'), scale, uploadsLastFrame, lastDrawMs, drawnFrames. A material that throws on 3 consecutive
frames sets status to { state: 'fallback', reason: 'material-error' } and stops drawing that surface only.
engine.createLayer(root, { scale?, under?, snapshots?, revealMs? }) (G7) draws every member in document order into
one canvas inserted as root's first child, z-index: -1 (root gets position: relative + isolation: isolate if it
is not already a stacking context); no eligibility filter, any descendant qualifies. under: true (G8, opt-in, off
by default) copies the layer's buffer before each member draws, so a later member's slg_under(screen) reads the
glass already drawn beneath it; snapshots: true (also opt-in) additionally exposes a downscaled last-frame copy
through slg_under to a floating ('own') surface over the layer. engine.registerBackdropSource({ id, paint(ctx,
region, scale, exclude), version(), covers? }) (G12) registers a private backdrop provider (e.g. Pro's pageScene),
referenced by SurfaceOptions.backdrop = { source: id }; repainted only on a version() change or when the surface's
view would leave the last painted strip, not every frame; a surface naming an id that registers later is wired up
once it appears. engine.capabilities() reports webgl, maxFragmentUniformVectors, maxTextureSize, bitmapTransfer,
tier ('full' | 'lite', a conservative heuristic).
engine.onFrame(callback, 'measure' | 'before' | 'after') hooks the shared frame loop; engine.invalidate(surfaces?)
marks surfaces dirty; engine.stats() reports { contexts, layers, surfaces, visible, drawn, missed, uploads,
uploadBytes, frameMs }.
Not implemented in this release: a frost input (no slg_frost) and pointer input (no slg_pointer) — there is no
pointer field anywhere in this API. An MIT example material is at tests/engine/tint-material.ts.

## Worker renderer (6.0)
import { createGlassHost } from 'simple-liquid-glass/next'. No React import; call it in the browser (an effect),
never on the server. The page describes glass as data and a renderer draws it: from a worker on canvases handed
over with transferControlToOffscreen where the browser supports WebGL there, on the page thread otherwise
({ thread: 'page' } forces that). Use it where glass must keep the display's rate while the page is busy or capped
(Chrome on Android gives a page 60 frames a second on a 120 Hz screen; a worker canvas gets 120), or for your own
GLSL material. The built entry's whole surface is in api/next.api.md in the repository.
const host = createGlassHost(); const layer = host.addLayer(canvas, { scale: 2 }) (the canvas's box is the layer:
size it with CSS, never width/height, and do not ask it for a context); layer.setBackdrop(await
createImageBitmap(picture), { rect?, fixed? }) hands over what the glass bends (the layer takes the bitmap);
layer.streamBackdrop(video) follows a playing video; layer.moveBackdrop({ rect, fixed }) moves the picture
without sending it again. const shape = layer.addShape({ x, y, width, height, radius }, { spring?, content?,
contentClip?, attributes? }); shape.set(box) springs there in the renderer, shape.set(box, { jump: true }) puts
it there; shape.setAttributes(values); shape.remove(). MAX_SHAPES is 24 per layer, each with up to 24 attributes.
A layer and its backdrop each move with the document (default) or stay in the viewport (fixed: true); glass
fixed over a scrolling page follows the scroll by itself. layer.status / onStatus(status, detail): 'unsupported'
means show your CSS fallback. A worker keeps MAX_WORKER_LAYERS (4) canvases; a fifth comes back 'unsupported'.
Materials: the built-in 'glass' (params: GLASS_LIGHT for the light tuning; lean: true for the cheaper variant) or
host.defineMaterial({ id, shade, field?, combine?, uniforms, textures?, bleed? }): GLSL defining vec4
slg_shade(vec2 p, vec3 field) with slg_screen(p), slg_backdrop(screen), slg_hasBackdrop(), slg_scale, slg_time,
slg_count, slg_boxes, slg_radii, slg_attributesA..F. layer.setParams({ name: value }) changes uniforms,
layer.setTexture(name, bitmap) fills a material texture, layer.setRunning(true) draws every frame for a material
that reads slg_time, layer.setBounds(rect) gives shapes walls. host.settle(), host.stats(), host.destroy().
reducedMotion is followed by default. A site whose CSP forbids blob: workers hosts simple-liquid-glass/next/worker
and passes workerUrl.
import { createGlassHost } from 'simple-liquid-glass/next/stack' adds: layer.stack(options) (another layer drawn
in the same canvas after the ones before it; its material reads the glass already there with vec4
slg_below(screen)), setClip(rect), setReach(px), setOrigin(x, y), setBare(true), setPace(ms), notify(redraw?)
and host.draw(). Its worker file is simple-liquid-glass/next/stack/worker.
Coming from 5.x: docs/migration.md ("v5.x → v6.0"). <LiquidGlass> and every other 5.x entry are unchanged.
